what: Which sends of a month also go out as an SMS. Team-wide, for every brand and every moment, beside holiday-cadence.json. A sale moment's arc gets an SMS on the beats listed here, each a twin of that beat's email: same date, same audience, same moment, same offer (the moment's named offer, checked against the bank like any other). A content moment gets none unless its key is listed under content_moments. The calendar plans SMS the same way whatever the brand's SMS platform (brands/<brand>/operations/brand.json `sms_platform`); the platform only decides where reads and, after a person's approval, the sends go. Nothing here sends or schedules anything.
why: the owner, 2026-11-03: SMS is part of the strategy; plan it once, read by every tool, same process for every brand, offer and moment. the owner, 2026-11-04: SMS is a companion to email, for reminders, engagement and getting people to respond.

beat_meaning.early-access: the arc's early-access send (VIP), when the month has one
beat_meaning.open: the arc's first offer-carrying send to everyone: the sale opens
beat_meaning.peak: the moment's own day (Black Friday on the 27th, a holiday on its date)
beat_meaning.last-chance: the arc's close: its last day, or the order-by date when the shipping record gives one

cap_rule: At most daily_cap SMS a day to any one segment. When two beats land on one day, the earlier one in `beats` is kept.

quiet_hours.rule: no SMS at or after `from`, or before `to`, in the recipient's own time zone

audience: SMS-consented members only: the beat's segment, sent only to the profiles in it that agreed to texts (both platforms enforce consent at send; the slot says so)

length.counts: the whole message, link and opt-out included

companion: An SMS is always the companion of an email in the plan, never a standalone campaign: it is planned only as the twin of an email send and names that email in `follows`; the email names it in `then` when it names nothing else. No new offer and no long copy: the email carries the argument, the text points at it.

job_meaning.reminder: the email's deadline or last day, in a line
job_meaning.engagement: a heads-up that something is open now — the beat says what (early access, or the sale itself)
job_meaning.reply: a two-way prompt (e.g. Reply YES for …): only where the brand's record names its reply keyword (operations/brand.json `sms_reply_keyword`) and its platform takes replies

reply_platforms.klaviyo: keyword replies through an SMS automation on a number that can receive texts (help.klaviyo.com, two-way SMS)
reply_platforms.postscript: custom keywords, US and Canada only (help.postscript.io, responding to subscribers)

beat_words.early-access: only this beat may say early access
beat_words.last-chance: only this beat may say last day, today only or ends today
beat_words.weekly: No new urgency: use only the companion email’s actual offer or useful point.

weekly.rule: One regular text per Monday–Sunday week, plus existing promotional reminders. Prefer Tuesday, paired with an existing email; never displace a reminder. The week belongs to the month containing Tuesday. Send at least one hour after its email, within quiet hours. Owner decision 2026-11-04.
